_comment: Headings and marker words written into the pool, in the pool language. Keys missing in another language fall back to these. 'm' = markers the agent must use verbatim.
readme_intro: Complete knowledge base about this person: identity, work history, concrete duties, achievements, skills, education, certifications, daily activity, writing style and narrative material. It is **not a CV**: it is raw material, as complete as possible, that any agent can read to know almost everything relevant about the person.
rule_sources: **Every fact has a source.** `[S001]` points to the sources index; `[J0001]` points to an entry of the activity journal.
rule_no_dup: **No duplicates, nothing lost.** Same information → only a new source tag. Information that completes an existing point → that point is enriched in place (the original sentences stay in the "Original text" sections). Contradicting information → both values are kept, marked as a conflict and listed in the open questions file until the person confirms.
rule_originals: **Original wording is kept.** Sentences from source documents are copied verbatim, in their language, into "Original text [S###]" sections, which are never edited or deleted.
rule_facts_claims: **Facts vs. claims.** Unconfirmed numbers or results are marked; inferences are labelled; values that must not be used again stay as history.
mk_conflict: two sources disagree; both values kept; listed in the open questions file
mk_inference: deduced, not stated by a source
mk_do_not_use: historical value or claim the person rejected; kept only as history
mk_private: visible to the person's own agents only; never shown to third parties (private repos, private details)
mk_as_of: fact that changes over time; the date says when it was true (history is kept)
how_to_add: Attach any file (CV, certificate, contract, reference letter, schedule, SOP, report, screenshot...) or tell the agent something, and say *"add to the knowledge pool"*. For daily activity, just tell what you did ("today I..."). For GitHub work: *"analyze my changes this week"*. The `pool-keeper` skill archives, extracts everything and merges it; the chat report is short, the full detail is in `CHANGELOG.md`.
desc_snapshot: One-page card (derived, regenerated after every ingest): current role, location, top skills, languages, availability, goals
desc_profile: Identity, contact, location, career targets, timeline
desc_experience: One file per position (job, internship, freelance, own business): context, duties, results, tools, original text
desc_skills: Skills, grouped, with evidence (where each was used)
desc_achievements: Achievement and numbers bank (A## IDs), across positions
desc_journal: Daily activity journal: one file per month, J#### entries, tag vocabulary in its README
desc_narrative_positioning: Headlines, summaries and positioning used so far (every variant kept)
desc_stories: STAR story bank (Situation, Task, Action, Result) for interviews and cover letters
desc_writing_style: How the person writes: observed patterns, active style rules (G###), correction log (K###)
desc_other: Projects, organisations, volunteering, references, interests, anything else
desc_goals: Short- and long-term goals, targets, learning goals (optional domain)
desc_availability: Availability, notice period, relocation, permits, work mode (optional domain)
desc_personal_life: Personal context the person chose to share (optional domain)
desc_keywords: Keyword → evidence index (to match job offers)
desc_open_questions: Information gaps, conflicts between sources, things asked and never done, answered questions
desc_changelog: History of every change to the pool
desc_sources: Archive of every source + index: original files with extracted text, chat notes, web research, delegated answers, GitHub notes
snapshot_note: Derived one-page card, regenerated after every ingest from the other files. Do not edit by hand; facts and sources live in the files it summarises.
ph_verbatim: verbatim sentence, in its original language
achievements_intro: Concrete achievements and results across positions, with an A## ID. Unconfirmed numbers carry `(needs confirmation)`.
journal_intro: Daily activities told by the person, one file per month (`YYYY-MM.md`). Every entry is a source in itself: `[J####]` is valid wherever `[S###]` is. Routine stays here; only new tools, measurable results, new responsibilities or role changes are promoted to the other files (with the `[J####]` tag).
ph_description: normalised description, in the pool language
journal_format_notes:
- IDs are global and incremental (`pk journal add` assigns them under a lock).
- Dates are absolute; an activity told days later carries `rec: YYYY-MM-DD` (the day it was recorded). A date that cannot be worked out → today's date + "(estimated date)".
- `@context` is the slug of an experience file, `@personal`, `@github:owner/repo`, or `@?` when unclear.
- The same action repeated = one entry with `qty:`.
- Third-party names are anonymised (role, not name).
- Scripts read the tokens of every built-in language (`qty:`/`jumlah:`/`cantidad:`, `rec:`/`dicatat`/`registrado:`, `link:`/`tautan:`/`enlace:`, `Original:`/`Asli:`, `Promoted:`/`Dipromosikan:`/`Promovido:`).
journal_vocab_intro: Reuse a tag before creating a new one. Aliases are other words that mean the same tag (searches and statistics resolve them).
narrative_intro: Headlines, summaries and angles used so far. Every variant is kept verbatim; the right one is chosen later, per offer.
stories_intro: Concrete situations told by the person or reconstructed from sources, ready for interviews and cover letters. Only facts with sources; inferences labelled. Format:
ws_intro: How this person writes in their own "formal" register. Any skill that writes on the person's behalf (CV, cover letter, LinkedIn, emails) **must** use it, so the result does not sound like generic AI prose.
ws_use_1: Read the active rules file **before** writing. Follow every rule with status `active` whose scope matches the document type and language.
ws_prio_1: rules from corrections (`Origin: K###`) — strongest, they come straight from the person
ws_prio_4: examples in the observed patterns file
ws_use_3: Use the observed patterns for example sentences, vocabulary and structure; never copy habits marked "do not imitate".
ws_use_4: Ignore rules with status `replaced by G###`.
ws_use_5: Facts (numbers, titles, dates) **always** come from the other pool files, never from the examples here.
ws_corrections: After another skill produced a text, the person can paste it together with the version they expected. The correction is logged (K###) and the active rules are updated automatically.
ws_desc_patterns: Patterns observed in documents the person wrote, per document type and dimension, with literal examples and sources
ws_desc_corrections: Correction history (K###): AI text, expected text, analysis, rules born from it
ws_patterns_intro: Extracted from texts the person wrote. Examples are quoted literally in their language. Newer sources weigh more. Recurring mistakes are recorded but marked "do not imitate".
ws_rules_intro: Rules other skills must follow when writing on the person's behalf. Priority: rules from corrections (`Origin: K###`) > higher Strength > rules from patterns. Ignore rules whose status is `replaced`. Format:
ws_corrections_intro: Every time the person pastes a text produced by an AI/skill together with the version they expected, the correction is logged here (newest first) and the active rules are updated. Format:
other_intro: Projects, organisations, volunteering, references, interests and anything that fits nowhere else.
optional_domain_note: Optional domain, enabled at setup. Only what the person chose to share; every fact with its source.
temporal_note: These facts change over time: write them with "as of <date>" and keep the previous values as history.
personal_note: Sensitive by nature: nothing here is shown to third parties unless the person asks; mark private items with 🔒.
keywords_intro: To match the keywords of an offer with evidence in the pool. Format: `keyword` → file / position.
oq_intro: What is still unknown or must be confirmed. Once answered, an item moves to "Answered" with its source tag. Answering is always optional.
oq_answer_file: write the answer under the question and say "process my answers".
not_done_intro: Things the person was asked about (e.g. by cv-tailor before a CV) and answered they have not done. Never ask again and never claim them.
kind_open_questions: Answers written in the open questions file
sources_intro: Every source is archived in `<YYYY-MM-DD>_<slug>/`: the original file + `extracted.txt`, or a notes file for chat notes, web research, delegated answers and GitHub syncs.
sources_journal_note: Journal entries (`J####`, activity journal folder) are sources too; they are not archived here.
